CA 91205. Meeting minutes will be available for viewing on the City Website at https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/departments/community-services-
parks/programs-services/senior-programs-services/senior-services-committee. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please
contact (818) 548-3715 during regular business hours.

PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES DURING THE MEETING.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon
request. Assisted listening devices are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for requests regarding sign
language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Community Services & Parks Administration Office, 613 E. Broadway, Room 120, Glendale, CA
91206.

minutes_text:
SENIOR SERVICES COMMITTEE

  REGULAR MEETING MINUTES
  Thursday, November 14, 2019, 3:00 p.m.
  Adult Recreation Center, 201 E. Colorado Street, Glendale, CA 91205

1.  ROLL CALL

  The meeting was called to order at 3:01 p.m.

  Present: Committee Members Barrios, Gano, Pierce, Varraveto, Torossian, Vice Chair Young, Chair
  Levee
  Absent: Committee Members Aintablian, Filipian, Gonzalez, Nazarian, Panchal, Voskanian
  Staff:  Aleksanian, Kavarian, Isayan, Moreno Hernandez

  A.  Report of Recording Secretary re: Posting of Agenda. Ms. Moreno Hernandez reported that the
  agenda for the November 14, 2019, quarterly meeting of the Senior Services Committee was
  posted on or before Monday, November 11, 2019, on the Bulletin Board outside City Hall.

2.  MINUTES
  A. Approval of the Minutes of the August 22, 2019, Senior Services Committee Meeting

  Moved: Varraveto  Second: Young
  Unanimous Consensus (Motion Carried)

3.  INTRODUCTIONS AND PRESENTATIONS
  A. Presentation on Public Works Dial-A-Ride and Beeline Services by Assistant Transit Manager Silva
  Baghdanian
  Silva Baghdanian, assistant transit manager with the City of Glendale’s Public Works department
  gave a presentation on senior-friendly transit options in the City of Glendale, including Beeline and
  Dial-A-Ride, and helpful tools to view bus schedules or plan a trip. Among some of the information
  she provided about Beeline is that all buses are ADA accessible, they connect to Metro, Metrolink,
  and Amtrak, and the fare is $0.50 for riders 62 years of age and older and for riders with
  disabilities. She said that bus schedule and trip planning information can be obtained at
  glendalebeeline.com; and the public can call (818) 548-3960 or email Beeline@glendaleca.gov
  with any questions. Ms. Baghdanian also made the following points about Dial-A-Ride: it’s for
  persons 65 years of age and older and/or with disabilities, it’s a curb-to-curb shared ride service
  that requires advanced reservations that can be made from 24 hours to 2 weeks in advance,
  standing reservations are available by subscription, the one-way fare is $1.50, a personal care
  attendant may ride for free, a ride to a City of Glendale meal site is free, and the service area
  includes Glendale, La Canada-Flintridge, La Crescenta, and Montrose. In response to Committee
  Member questions, Ms. Baghdanian stated that these transportation services are funded by local
  return Measure M and R funds and some federal assistance; call-in hours are Monday- Thursday,
  7:30 a.m. – 5:30 p.m. and Fridays 8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.; and Beeline accepts Tap cards.

  Ms. Baghdanian invited all Committee Members and staff to go outside for a demonstration of a
  Beeline bus and a Dial-A-Ride van.
 4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  None

5.  Reports – Information Only
  A. Senior Programs and Events Update for Fall 2019
  Community Services Supervisor Aylin Isayan gave a PowerPoint presentation about the following
  programs and events for seniors that took place in the fall: Connect Hearing check-up, LA Metro
  Mobile Customer Service, On the Move Riders Program, Wild West Senior Luncheon, AARP
  Driving Safety, Senior Seminar, Flu Shots, and Senior Luncheon Halloween Celebration.

Committee Member Pierce left the meeting at 3:43 p.m., at which point a quorum of the Committee
was lost. Staff proceeded with providing a report for the remaining agenda items, but no action was
taken by the Committee.
6.  Action Items
  A.  Program Evaluation of Emergency Preparedness event held on October 5, 2019
  1.  Motion to provide feedback on 2019 Emergency Preparedness Event
  Sr. Community Supervisor Maggie Kavarian gave a PowerPoint presentation with an overview
  of the Emergency Preparedness event, including the 12 Steps Task List, presentations and
  speakers, Senior Lunch Program, raffle prizes, and fiscal impact, which was around $5,600.

  Chair Levee commented that should we have the event again, we wouldn’t have to pay for the
  banners again. Vice Chair Young said that she wasn’t happy with the stamp used at the event.
  Committee Member Varraveto said that people visited her table multiple times to get
  giveaways, but that the stamp helped. Ms. Torrosian said she thought the event had a great
  set-up and that it was great that each table had giveaways. Ms. Kavarian recognized
  Committee Member Gonzalez for assisting with planning the event. Chair Levee asked that
  this item be continued to the next meeting so that the Committee can provide feedback and
  start planning the next event early; she requested that staff have potential dates and a location
  ready by next meeting. Committee Member Gano said that the Fire Department will have an
  emergency manager by December or January, and that with the manager on board, the Fire
  Department will have a budget for such events. Deputy Director of Community Services &
  Parks Aleksanian said that it would be better to hold the event at a Community Services &
  Parks location in the future, maybe at the Civic Auditorium, to facilitate set-up/breakdown.
  No action was taken due to lack of quorum.

  B.  Senior Scam Stoppers Event
  1.  Motion to provide feedback regarding the Senior Scam Stoppers event
  Ms. Kavarian reported that Glendale Police Department, Community Services & Parks, and
  WISE & Healthy Aging are coordinating a Senior Scam Stoppers event to take place on
  January 28, 2020, 9:30 a.m. – 12:30 p.m., and asked the Committee to promote it. She said
  that the event will include speakers and lunch for seniors; GTV6 will be televising it Live. Chair
  Levee said to keep in mind that there was a glitch with Dial-A-Ride at the Emergency
  Preparedness event.
  No action was taken due to lack of quorum.
7.  COMMITTEE/STAFF COMMENTS
  Chair Levee said that a master plan for aging will be presented to the governor in March 2020, which
  may guide the Committee’s actions. Ms. Kavarian said that the City of Glendale participated in the
  master planning process.
  Chair Levee asked staff for an update on the resource guide that the Committee voted to put together
  in May. Ms. Isayan said that staff changes in her section have caused a delay, but that they are now
  working to complete it.
8.  ADJOURNMENT
  The meeting was adjourned at 4:10 p.m.
